This is a short clickable game. There is no written response. Complete all three levels, then continue to the Life Checkpoint.
:::

## Open the game

### Fastest method

1. Click **[PLAY CIRCUIT QUEST IN JUPYTERLITE](https://jupyter.org/try-jupyter/lab/index.html?fromURL=https%3A%2F%2Fandrewandrade.ca%2Ftech-edu-resources%2Fassets%2Ftej-computational%2Fnotebooks%2F09a-circuit-quest.ipynb){target="_blank"}**.
2. Choose **Python (Pyodide)** if Jupyter asks for a kernel.
3. Run the collapsed setup cell with **Shift+Enter**.
4. Run **Start Circuit Quest**.
5. Play the board that appears below the cell.

### Download and upload method

If the direct link does not open the notebook:

1. Download [Circuit Quest (`.ipynb`)](../../assets/tej-computational/notebooks/09a-circuit-quest.ipynb).
2. Open **[JupyterLite](https://jupyter.org/try-jupyter/lab/){target="_blank"}**.
3. Select **Upload Files** and choose `09a-circuit-quest.ipynb`.
4. Double-click the uploaded file and choose **Python (Pyodide)**.

## How to play

1. Click a blue wire tile to rotate it.
2. Trace the path from the battery.
3. Connected tiles glow green.
4. Light every lamp to finish the level.
5. Use **Hint** or **Reset level** whenever you need them.

The game contains three small levels:

| Level | Goal |
|---|---|
| 1. One turn to power | Rotate one wire and light one lamp. |
| 2. Route around the corner | Build a complete path through a 3 by 3 grid. |
| 3. Power two lamps | Rotate a junction and power two branches. |

::: {.callout-note title="The setup code is collapsed"}
You do not need to understand the whole game engine. Run it once. The game is an example of what Python can build from variables, lists, functions, conditions, loops, and button events.
:::

## What the game teaches

- A lamp needs a complete path to the source.
- A rotated wire can create an open circuit.
- A junction can send current into more than one branch.
- A program can test every connection and provide immediate feedback.

After the game, continue to the [Life Checkpoint Upgrade](midterm-circuit-investigation.qmd).

## Troubleshooting

| Problem | Fix |
|---|---|
| No board appears | Run the collapsed setup cell, then run **Start Circuit Quest** again. |
| Buttons appear as plain text | Select **Python (Pyodide)** as the kernel. |
| A lamp stays off | Follow the green path and rotate the first blue tile after it. |
| You cannot find the mistake | Select **Hint**. |
| You want to start over | Select **Reset level**. |
| The browser was closed | Reopen or upload the notebook and run both game cells again. |

## Source note

The activity adapts the rotating-tile idea used by circuit-path and Netwalk-style puzzles. It uses `ipywidgets`, which is included in the official Try Jupyter Python environment. The circuit levels and notebook implementation are original course materials.
